S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms that develop in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor, usually beginning within a short time after the event and causing distress or functional impairment out of proportion to what would be expected. The presentation is stress-linked and time-limited rather than a primary mood, anxiety, trauma-related, or psychotic disorder, and symptoms typically improve as the person adapts or the stressor resolves.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Nicholas Foley’s older sister moved back into the family home with her newborn after a difficult breakup, turning his already busy household into a crowded, unpredictable place just as he was balancing mechanic training, part-time shop work, and college assignments. During the following month he found his usual mix of budgeting, guitar practice, maker projects, and pickup basketball harder to keep steady because his reactions to the new family demands kept spilling into school and work. The impairment was noticeable but limited: he remained engaged, though he missed deadlines and stepped back from a community theater set project he had been excited about. He brought it up himself during a routine campus advising appointment, and the adviser helped him schedule an assessment through the student counseling service.

S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since my sister and her baby moved back home, I’ve been more on edge and down than usual, snapping over little stuff at the house and then showing up to class or the shop already drained, so I’m still getting by but I’ve missed a couple deadlines and backed out of helping with the theater set because I couldn’t keep everything straight.

add_requirements.Symptoms must develop within 3 months of: I was doing okay before my sister and the baby moved in, and the trouble started within a couple weeks of the house getting crowded.
add_requirements.Within 6 months of the termination of th: The situation hasn’t really ended yet—my sister and her newborn are still living with us—so this is all still tied to the same change at home.
